channel.title: Phantom Entry
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Phantom Entry" - An anomalous Security Containment Procedure entry in the foundation's database, suddenly appearing out of nowhere.

item.title: Re: Phantom Entry
item.content:encoded:
Oh my, thank you for the response!

So to begin with, this is not really like, an "anti meme" kind of "anti meme". It's a piece of entry in the database, perfectly readable, perfectly manipulatable, but the content DESCRIBES it as an anti meme, with the help of the entity claiming that it is. The actual entry itself isn't antimemetic, the content only CLAIMS that it is. This happens because documentation happens side by side with research, as requested by the entity because it is sating our curiosity to its amusement. Then after it departed, everyone involved instantly forgets everything and has each of their "unreadable" memory filled with vague fabrications, but the SCP entry remains, fully authorized and reviewed even. Hence, the "anomality" of the situation, where the containment procedure is supposed to be executed, none of the staff mentioned in the entry responded, resulting in disciplinary actions, but then turning into an immediate confusion fiesta where no one remembers about it, resulting in the proposal that the entry is anomalous.

Remember, this SCP is not really all just about the content of the anomalous entry, it's also about the validity of the entry, as it's at the end of the day just another documentation, only with no evidence. So this could be an anomaly in the system, maybe a security overlook and some rando messed with the database, possible sabotage, drunk researcher, who knows?

In the entry, the foundation really doesn't do much but interviews at first, since the entity creates the first impression of being another reluctant reality hopper, hence being treated as such. Standard Humanoid chamber, all that stuff. Each entry, the foundation catches it roaming more and more, sometimes suddenly in other SCP chambers, disappear from its own the room, interacting more and more to the point of making people uncomfortable and disturbed. Every time it does questionable things, it gets hit with another interview, and as the entry goes on this cycle will get deeper and deeper as it straight up appears in Keter facilities, roam outside of the protected area, "accidentally" causing a breach, speaks more aggressively, lose its charming attitude, etc etc. Basically, it's character changes questionably each passing day, and the foundation will be conflicted to take action as each misbehavioural instance caused no casualty, but is still dangerous until it goes so severe the foundation gets extremely desperate (where it gets a Keter label and is clearly uncontainable), and at the peak of mass panic, the entity settles down, reveals what it has been up to which is a research of its own, and went adios. There ends the entry.

But again, very important to note that this is an SCP entry about an SCP entry, which plays a huge part in the informational horror element, as viewers as left with a lot of doubt and questions regarding the entry. The actual, non-content entry will be very passive and boring because it really is just about a random documentation with no proof but is able to have so much authenticity in written permission, authorization, all the legal shenanigans. It basically will have weird pacing that kicks the readers in the end, saying "hey maybe all of that was lie lol".

item.title: Re: Phantom Entry
item.content:encoded:
So like…what does this article look like? How are you intending showing the transition from 'lighthearted slice of life reality hopping Mary Sue' into 'a dreadful, cosmic horror-esque atmosphere'?

My concern is it feels like the core anomaly here is somewhat complex and like…also kinda generically has the feel of an antimeme; and I think what you want to do is interesting enough that it could work but I don't really have a feel for how the article is telling this story or how the story is paced; and my concern is that it might end up feeling very passive cos it doesn't really feel like the PoV characters (i.e. the foundation) are doing much to get us from the start to the end?

item.title: Phantom Entry
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Emotional, Comedy, Mystery

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: An SCP entry about an anomalous SCP entry.

Central Narrative: Out of nowhere, a new fully authorized SCP entry has appeared randomly in the Foundation's database, where it describes an entity so foreign and alien to the current local reality, where any and all sophisticated informational stimuli regarding it cannot be transcribed and comprehended when unaided, resulting in the immediate loss of said information after it removes its presence, such as memory. Translations, however, are perfectly comprehensible, such as written or recorded materials. However, it may also be corrupted if said entity acts upon it. The entity refers to itself in the English language as "Your Warden" or "Them", a being that proclaimed itself as the safe keeper of all reality from itself, by destroying realities beyond repair, and cleaning those near broken. However, even with all the SCP shenanigans, the time it spent observing the world(s) in this local reality had changed its mind, and coming to the absurd conclusion that the SCP universe may be the most convoluted, but it is far from broken, and everything belongs, resulting in its departure leaving this reality to its own business.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mass confusion where absolutely no one remembers anything regarding the Security Containment Procedure ever transpiring adds to the curiosity of the reader, and it also enjoys the treatment of a drastic mood change, it slowly shifts from being a lighthearted slice of life reality hopping Mary Sue into a dreadful, cosmic horror-esque atmosphere. The horror will be mostly informational horror, the feeling of dread when presented absurd consensuses and information. There's just too much out there, and you have no say over it. The struggle to understand will lead to hatred, fear, confusion, denial, and much more will be explored.
